transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because when I even think there might be a bat, or something flapping around in the stockroom, I get scared right away. My heart kind of jumps, I start sweating, and I feel like I have to get out of there immediately.
Is it just bats that trigger this fear, or are there other things that cause a similar reaction?

Mostly bats, yeah. But it can be anything that looks like one, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway. I know in my head a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but in that moment my mind reacts like I’m in real danger.
How often do you find yourself thinking about bats or worrying about encountering one when you're not in a situation where they might be present?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think about them all the time or anything. It’s more if something reminds me of them, or if I know I’m going near a place where one could be. Then I start worrying about it.
Do you worry about other animals or situations that might not be directly related to bats?

Not really other animals, no. It’s mostly bats or things that look like them. Like I know a bat in the store probably wouldn’t hurt me, but if I see a quick flutter in the back hallway, my brain just reacts like I’m in real danger.
Do you think your fear would decrease if you were in a situation where you knew for certain there were no bats present?

Yeah, I think so. If I really knew there were no bats there, I’d probably calm down some. But if I see something that looks like one, or even just a quick flutter, my mind still kind of jumps to danger before I can think it through.
Do you ever find yourself avoiding places or situations because of your fear, even if there's no obvious connection to bats?

Yeah, I do. At work I’ve been trading away closing shifts when I can, because that’s when I’m more nervous about it. I also take the long way around the loading area instead of going through there.

If I have to check the stairwell, I still do it, but I kind of rush through it, holding my phone, and I’m scared the whole time.
Has your fear of bats affected your relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Yeah, mostly with my daily life and work goals. My manager has started asking if I can really handle being a shift lead, because I keep trying to trade out of closing duties and I’m not as dependable with the after-hours checks.

That’s been hard, because I was working toward a permanent management position, and now it feels like this could mess that up.
Do you think you would be afraid of being in a dark or enclosed space even if you knew there were no bats present?

I’m not really sure. I mean, dark or enclosed places can make me a little uneasy sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it fear by itself. It’s more that my mind goes to, “What if there’s a bat in here?” If I truly knew there weren’t any, I think I’d probably be okay.
Are there any other specific objects or situations, aside from bats, that trigger a similar intense fear response in you?
No, not that I can think of. It’s really bats that set me off like that. Other things might make me a little uncomfortable, but not in the same way.
Do you think your fear would be triggered by something that doesn't resemble a bat but is still an animal that flies?

Not really just any flying animal, no. If it doesn’t look like a bat, I don’t think it hits me the same way. But if I see something that looks like one, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway, my mind kind of jumps to “bat,” and then it feels like danger, even though I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me.
Do you think you could be afraid of another animal if you believed it was present in the same situation where you usually fear bats?

Maybe, but only if I thought it was a bat or something like one. I know a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I see a quick flutter back in the hallway, my mind just treats it like I’m in real danger. Another animal wouldn’t really do that unless I mistook it for a bat.
Would your fear be triggered if you thought there was another animal, not a bat, that could potentially be in the stockroom or a similar place?

Not really, no. If I knew it was some other animal and not a bat, I don’t think I’d react the same way. It’s more when I see something that looks like a bat, or just a quick flutter back there, my mind jumps to “bat” and I feel like I’m in danger, even though I know it probably isn’t going to hurt me.
Would you feel afraid if you thought there was a different animal, not a bat, in the stockroom?

No, not if I knew it was some different animal. It’s really the bat part that gets me. Like, I know a bat in the store probably wouldn’t hurt me, but if I see something that looks like one, or just a quick flutter back in the hallway, my mind treats it like I’m in real danger.
Would your fear be triggered if you were in a situation where you thought there might be an animal, but you weren't sure what kind of animal it was?

Yeah, if I wasn’t sure what it was and I saw something fluttering or moving quick, especially back in the hallway, I’d probably think “bat” right away. I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me, but my mind kind of treats it like I’m in real danger.
Would your fear be triggered if you thought there might be an unknown animal in the stockroom, without knowing what it was?

Yeah, if I didn’t know what it was and I saw something that looked like a bat, or even just a quick flutter back there, it would set me off. I know a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but in that moment my mind acts like I’m in real danger.
Would your fear be triggered by the possibility of any unknown animal being present, not just a bat?

Not any unknown animal, really. It’s more if I think it could be a bat — like if I see something flutter fast or something that looks like one in the back hallway. I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me, but in that moment my mind treats it like I’m in danger.
Would your fear be triggered by the uncertainty of what animal might be present, regardless of whether it's a bat or not?

No, not just any animal. It’s really when I think it might be a bat. Like, I know a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I see something that looks like one or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway, my mind treats it like I’m in real danger.
Would you feel anxious or fearful if you were in a situation where you knew an animal was present, but you had no idea what kind of animal it was?

If I knew there was some animal but didn’t know what kind, I’d be nervous mainly if there was a chance it was a bat. Like, if I saw something small move fast or flutter in the back hallway, my mind would jump to that. I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me in the store, but it still feels dangerous in the moment.
Would your fear be triggered by the presence of an unknown animal, without any resemblance to a bat?

No, not if it doesn’t seem like a bat. If it’s just some unknown animal, that’s not really what sets me off. It’s when I see something that looks like a bat, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway, that my mind suddenly treats it like I’m in danger, even though I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me.
